e.etymology: A spelling of Ayla, which is both a Turkish name for the halo of light around the moon and a form of Hebrew Elah, oak or terebinth. The double l spelling is common in Brazil.

e.meaning: navy: a fleet of ships, and the dark blue color
e.etymology: A phonetic respelling of Navy, the English word for a fleet and for the dark blue of naval uniforms, which became a girls' name around 2020.
A girl's name used mainly in Pakistani families. Its meaning is not well established.
The French feminine of Jean (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. It is the French name of Joan of Arc, Jeanne d'Arc.
namesakes: Joan of Arc (Jeanne d'Arc, French heroine and saint)
Jeanne Tripplehorn (actress in Basic Instinct and Big Love)

e.etymology: A Spanish blend of Maria and Celia, also spelled Maricela. It is most common in Mexico and among Mexican Americans.
An American spelling of Arabic Shakil, handsome or well-formed. It rose and fell with the career of basketball star Shaquille O'Neal.
namesakes: Shaquille O'Neal (NBA Hall of Fame center)

assoc.t: Shaquille O'Neal, NBA legend known as Shaq

e.etymology: A spelling of Serena, from Latin serenus, clear and calm. Serina is also a separate Japanese girls' name written with various kanji.
An Irish surname, an English form of O Caireallain, best known from comedian George Carlin. For girls it is also read as a blend of Carly or Carla and Lynn.

e.meaning: pet form of Caroline, Calista and other Cal- names
e.etymology: A spelling of Callie, a pet form of Caroline, Calista and other Cal- names. In Greek names such as Calliope and Calista the root is kallos, beauty.
The English word, from Latin passio, suffering, which first named the Passion of Christ and later came to mean intense feeling.
From Sanskrit ashvin, possessing horses, from ashva, horse. The Ashvins are the twin horsemen gods of the Vedas, and Ashvin is a month of the Hindu calendar.

e.meaning: the country India, named for the River Indus
e.etymology: A modern spelling of India, the country name, which comes through Greek and Latin from the River Indus.
namesakes: Indya Moore (actor in the TV series Pose)

e.etymology: A one-n spelling of Danny used in French and Spanish, the pet form of Daniel, from Hebrew Daniyel, God is my judge.
Used as a spelling of Cash, with the look of the English word cache, a hidden store, from French cacher, to hide. Cache is also a valley and county in northern Utah.
e.note: The word cache is said KASH, but the name is sometimes misread as ka-SHAY.

e.etymology: From Arabic malih, beautiful, charming or graceful, in its feminine form.
A modern American name, a variant of Kamari with the -auri spelling seen in Jamauri and Amauri.
A pet form of Sullivan, from the Irish surname O Suileabhain, usually read as little dark-eyed one.

assoc.t: Sulley, the big blue monster in Monsters, Inc.
Sully Sullenberger, Miracle on the Hudson pilot

e.note: As an English verb, to sully means to stain or tarnish.

e.etymology: A pet form of Esther in Yiddish-speaking families, and in English of Henrietta and other -etta names.
A modern American name in the family of Kamari and Amori.
A modern American coinage that joins Ace to the -lyn ending, with the rhythm of Jocelyn and Gracelyn.
The Italian word for tomorrow, from Latin de mane, in the morning. Its use as a name grew after rapper T.I.'s son Domani appeared on the family's reality show from 2011.
A modern American name that crosses Javon with Giovanni, the Italian form of John.
In Hebrew, from gal, wave, and Yah, a short form of God's name. Galia is also used in Spanish-speaking countries and, as Galya, is the Russian pet form of Galina.
Probably a phonetic spelling of Eilidh, the Scottish Gaelic form of Helen, said AY-lee, or a sister to Eily, an Irish pet form of Eileen.
From Arabic sa'diyya, fortunate or happy, the feminine of Sa'di, from sa'd, good fortune.
The English word for a small stream, from Middle English creke. It follows River, Brooks and Ridge among outdoor names for boys.

assoc.t: the Creek (Muscogee) Nation of the American Southeast

e.etymology: A modern Indian boys' name, also spelled Viaan; actress Shilpa Shetty chose that spelling for her son in 2012.
From Persian mah, moon, and the suffix -sa, like. The death of Mahsa Amini in Iranian police custody in 2022 set off protests around the world.

assoc.t: Mahsa Amini, whose 2022 death sparked Iran's protests

e.etymology: From the Ge'ez word nolawi, shepherd, used in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church for Christ the Good Shepherd.
A K spelling of Cassian, from Latin Cassianus, a derivative of the Roman family name Cassius. Saint John Cassian was a 5th-century monk; Cassian Andor leads the Star Wars series Andor.
From Punjabi jind, life or soul, a word of Persian origin. Maharani Jind Kaur was the last queen of the Sikh Empire.
